what: Phase 2 (roll references, hip line, ankle grounding) acceptance metrics on the client take, fix round.

variants.before: _ROLL_WEIGHT = 0 + the lowest-mesh-vertex grounding (the shipped pre-Phase-2 build; bit-identical away from _align's antipodal branch, see rollback note)

gates_were_restated.1_continuity: The brief's ship gate 'max consecutive-frame roll change <= 15 deg' is ACCEPTED AS UNMET and is no longer a gate. The captured bend normal itself moves up to 55.7 deg between consecutive stop-motion poses and the pre-Phase-2 build already fails the gate by a wider margin than the fix does, so the number measures the take, not the retarget. Reference smoothing (pose3d/geometry/retarget.py) was deliberately NOT added: it would re-introduce the cross-pose blending Phase 1 removed and measurement showed it moves upper_arm.L by 1.5 deg and makes forearm.L worse. Restated gate: roll error 0 deg median AND max on the frames where the bend plane exists (bend >= 40 deg), plus the synthetic straightening-sweep continuity test (tests/test_retarget.py::test_roll_is_continuous_across_a_straightening_limb).
gates_were_restated.2a_roll_ceiling: The <= 15 deg roll-error max ceiling applies where bend >= 40 deg. The 20/40 ramp withholds roll authority by design on nearly straight limbs, so the residual on those frames is recorded separately (roll_error_ramped_frames_deg) and not gated.
gates_were_restated.2b_hand: The 'hand.L posed-axis spread <= 40 deg' bound is replaced by 'hand roll spread reduced'. The hand bone has no aim of its own and inherits the forearm verbatim, and the CAPTURED forearm swing is itself ~112 deg, so its axis spread cannot fall near 40 deg however its roll behaves.
gates_were_restated.2c_ground: The ground-datum gate applies to the character's own ankle over the grid. The audit's dz-vs-capture definition (captured ankle z minus the character's lowest vertex) is recorded but not gated: its residual is ankle RETARGET error, which Phase 2 does not address.

notes.max_consecutive_frame_roll_change_deg: METRIC, NOT A GATE (ruling 1). Definition: each bone's posed roll about its own aim axis, measured against a fixed world gauge (+Z projected perpendicular to the aim), unwrapped, max |change| between consecutive frames. This definition is comparable between `before` and `after`; the audit's 'change in the applied correction' is 0.0 for every bone in `before` by construction and cannot be compared at all. The take is 26 discrete stop-motion poses, so frame-to-frame continuity is not a property the data has.
notes.roll_convention: Roll is a MEASUREMENT for upper_arm.* and thigh.* (the elbow and the knee are hinges, so the bend plane fixes the parent bone's spin) and a CONVENTION for forearm.* and shin.* — pronation and shin twist are never observed and there are no hand or foot keypoints. A 0.0 deg forearm roll error is not accuracy.
notes.rollback: _ROLL_WEIGHT = 0 restores the pre-roll matrices bit for bit EXCEPT at _align's antipodal (c < -0.999999) branch, where the rest reference now makes the axis pick deterministic (F43). That branch is deliberately no longer arbitrary.
notes.sole_tilt: Recorded, never asserted: the shin of this rigid-footed mannequin genuinely tilts 16-86 deg and levelling the sole would replace a measurement with a convention.
notes.mesh_below_grid_pct: The accepted cost of an ankle datum with an unlevelled sole: a tilted foot now crosses the plane instead of the whole scene bobbing. Bounded by tests/test_view_orientation.py::test_grounding_is_ankle_based.

hand_roll_spread_reduced.definition: the hand bone inherits the forearm's matrix verbatim, so its roll IS the forearm's: signed angle, about the posed forearm axis, between the carried rest bend reference and the CAPTURED SHOULDER LINE projected perpendicular to that axis; spread = max deviation from the take's circular mean. The gauge is body-fixed on purpose — a world-fixed gauge folds the subject's torso yaw into 'roll' and reads 44.6 -> 47.6 deg (hand_roll_spread_world_gauge_deg).
hand_roll_spread_reduced.caveat: Ruling 2b quotes 94.8 -> 58.9 deg from the Phase 2 report, whose definition of 'hand roll spread' was never recorded; it could not be reproduced here (eight candidate definitions were tried). The definition above is stated in full so the number is auditable. The RULING — that the bound is 'reduced', not an absolute ceiling — is what is applied.

hand_axis_spread_context.why: the axis spread cannot fall near the brief's 40 deg: the hand has no aim of its own and the CAPTURED forearm already swings this much.
